newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: DARWIN LASHED BY TROPICAL LOW
The Weather Bureau in Darwin expects to be naming a tropical low as a cyclone later this morning.
Darwin is already being buffeted by winds gusting to about 80 kilometres an hour and has 135 millimetres of rain since yesterday morning.
The low is moving northwest across the Timor Sea at five kilometres an hour and was last reported to be centred 25 kilometres from Melville Island's Snake Bay.
A cyclone warning remains current for coastal and island communities between Crocker Island and Cape Fourcroy.
A cyclone watch extends south to the Daly River mouth including Darwin and from Wyndham to Kuri Bay in Western Australia.
David Thomas of the Weather Bureau says Melville and Bathurst Islands are probably in for high winds, but at this stage damaging gales are not expected to hit the coast.
APPEAL FOR SYMPATHY IN SAUDI MURDER CASE
The lawyer representing the two British women accused of killing an Australian nurse in Saudi Arabia says he may appeal to the victim's family to have mercy on the accused.
Lawyer, Salah al-Hujeilan, says he'll make his decision after speaking to his clients on Saturday.
Lucille McLauchlan, 31, of Dundee and Deborah Parry, 41, from the Midlands, are accused of murdering 55-year-old Yvonne Gilford from South Australia on December the 11th at a hospital in Dharan.
Mr al-Hujeilan says under Islamic law, it's up to the victim's family to demand that capital punishment be considered by the judge.
He says he will appeal directly to the Gilford family not to ask for the death penalty if his clients are found guilty.
EXTENSION TO BONDI RAIL PLANNED
The New South Wales government will advertise at the end of this month for expressions of interest in building the Bondi Beach rail link.
The project requires a 3-kilometre extension of the Eastern Suburbs Railway line, opened by the Wran government in 1979.

Transport Minister Brian Langton says at this stage there are two proposed routes, each commencing at Bondi Junction, travelling underground along either a Bondi Road or Birrell Street route, and finishing at an underground station at the southern end of Bondi Beach.
Mr Langton says studies show construction could be completed in about two and a half years.
ALGAE AT SYDNEY BEACHES
Rafts of red algae bloom which can cause skin irritations have been found at Manly and Whale beaches in Sydney's north.
Peter Yates of the Environment Protection Authority says the algae is non-toxic but can irritate the skin of some people and animals.
Mr Yates says EPA tests confirm the algae is Noctiluca scintillans, a common species, and not the type known as Chattonella, the "red tide".
He advises people to avoid contact with the algal blooms.
CAUSTIC SODA LEAKAGE AT QLD REFINERY

Environment department officers are investigating a caustic soda leakage at Queensland Alumina Limited's Gladstone refinery. In a statement released yesterday, A Q-A-L spokesman says an incident within the plant caused the discharge of a quantity of Caustic Soda.
The leakage was mostly contained by an on-site system in two ponds on the plant's western side, however a small amount overflowed into an adjacent small pond on company property.
The spokesman says a number of small fish died as a result of the accident, but there was no damage to the harbour marine environment.
An internal investigation of plant operating procedures has been launched, and Department of Environment officers have investigated the spill.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
